acceptance_criteria: Startup readiness, provider search, entity search, context assembly, breaker, and timeout outcomes map to one bounded generated memory-capability vocabulary.
Disabled, required-unavailable, optional-degraded, ready, stale, missing-evidence, recovering, and recovered states have explicit non-overlapping health semantics.
A provider or context failure cannot become a successful empty-context observation, and insufficient evidence cannot read healthy.
Health exposes last attempt, last success, consecutive failure, oldest failure, recovery, and evidence coverage through bounded content-free fields.
Restart rehydrates or conservatively resets memory-capability evidence so prior failure cannot silently become a healthy green.
Probe cadence and freshness are bounded, avoid request-amplified provider calls, and cover both memory and entity search modes.
Health and alerts contain no index host, project identifier, query, filter, identity, record ID, content, credential, or raw exception.
End-to-end tests cover startup classification, runtime failures, empty success, breaker open and recovery, timeouts, stale evidence, restart, and health serialization.
blast_radius: Startup gating, Pinecone authentication and project guard, memory and entity search, context assembly, chat responses, consolidation enablement, runtime and top-level health, alerts, restart evidence, operator recovery, and public health privacy.
evidence_summary: Three body-free live reads agreed on the open issue identity, empty labels, update time, URL, 12,307-byte body length, and body hash while API and SSH main both resolved to the exact pin. Exact main performs one Pinecone readiness probe during startup and logs its state, but does not pass that state or a refreshable memory-capability reader to the health server. A failed startup probe only prevents consolidation from starting; chat enrichment is enabled by a nonempty index string, and runtime health can remain healthy with no successful memory evidence. Search and entity-search failures are converted to empty result sets with status and raw error data discarded by loadContext. The chat runtime separately converts rejected or timed-out context retrieval to null and continues, but records no bounded outcome, consecutive-failure count, freshness, or recovery transition. Chat health observes queue and enrichment timing only, so startup auth, index, project, network, breaker, retrieval, and context-loss states remain absent after restart and during turns. The exact-pin union falsifier run passed 455 of 455 tests across ten files with no skips; readiness tests stop at startup classification and health tests contain no end-to-end memory-capability contract. Three complete stable open-PR captures each enumerated 32 PRs, 26 drafts, 36 changed-file pages, 32 closing-reference pages, and 1,152 file rows with digest 0b0a74fc0fe95b70e7c03b96002dac4708e3cf9a0324bb553527f8ce69db0995. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The remaining finding is falsified when context assembly consumes detailed provider outcomes, preserves bounded failure and freshness across restart, and projects required/optional memory capability into health without allowing failed empty context to read green.
impact: Instances can advertise healthy chat service while memory authentication, index selection, project isolation, network access, breaker state, retrieval, or context assembly is unavailable. Operators cannot distinguish intentionally empty context from silent memory loss, cannot see persistent degradation across turns or restart, and cannot verify recovery.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read issues #2572 and #2570 plus both API and SSH main immediately before integration.

Choose probe cadence, freshness, restart rehydration, aggregation, and recovery-clearing semantics before implementation.
Add RED and GREEN startup, provider, context, breaker, timeout, stale, missing-evidence, restart, recovery, health, alert, and privacy tests.
Re-scan every open PR and establish one implementation owner before mutation.
Run startup, provider, context, chat runtime, consolidation, health, alert, restart, runbook, and publication checks on committed implementation bytes.
